clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's house every evening; your father took night shifts and stayed away from home; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and was warned at work; your mother lay awake over them; your brother Callum had ear infections through the winter. The conflict between Delphine and your aunt Simone over the house is undated and struck out. Each shift but the last falls in the months after the death; Callum's infections run through the winter, and Delphine took a job at the library by May 1979, where things settled.

clusters.name: your mother's bed rest, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bed rest in March 1984, within months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep the house and overfunctioned; your father argued with his mother over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it; your own anxiety rose, though the month is uncertain and this shift is struck out. Three shifts that count sit close in those months around a change in your mother's functioning, and the trouble settled after your sister Ines was born in September.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, within a decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news of her; she had a bad fall and walked with a frame; her new medicine steadied her for a while; your father argued with your uncle Lyle over who should help their parents; your grandfather had chest pains; Hazel could no longer dress herself; your mother took her to the clinic twice a week; your aunt Mavis came to stay one week in four to nurse her; your father drank most evenings; your aunt Pearl had panic spells at the wheel. Hazel had a good summer in 1994, but the shifts in her functioning continued to fall away, each one followed by another in her household. The trouble reaches to June 1997 when Hazel moved to the nursing home and your father cut his drinking back to weekends, where things settled into a new balance.

clusters.name: Callum's move north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for a job up north in May 1999, within months before and after: your father argued with him most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; you skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took you with her everywhere, even to work; you were back at school full days and passed your exams by August 2000. Each shift but one falls in the months around his departure, and the trouble settled once you were back at school.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within months: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; you took a job at the garden centre and slept through the night again by November. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then. The trouble settled when you took the job and your functioning rose.
